place.source_title: William T. Bonniwell House, Wauwatosa Avenue

brief: Long two-storey side-gabled frame house of the 1830s-40s (HABS dates it 'after 1830') in the Milwaukee River mill village of Thiensville: plain clapboard walls, regular rows of 6/6 windows, a simple entrance with a small sign board over it, interior chimneys and a low foundation, half hidden by big trees. HABS drawings record the plans and framing.

floors: W W W W W W
W W W D W W
facade.notes: a long two-storey side-gabled house with flush or plastered walls, six bays a floor, a centre entrance under a small entablature, plain cornice; overgrown with trees and shrubs to the eaves: a worn, half-abandoned farm house (HABS 1930s)

why.note: the two-storey, one-room-deep farmhouse; here stretched to six bays
a 1840 house left behind by the farm economy: overgrowth closing in
